title: Append-only streaming commit protocol for bulk embedding ingestion
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement an append-only streaming commit protocol and lightweight async job API to support large-scale embedding ingestion with strong idempotency, deterministic ordering at the batch level, and efficient retries. This ticket covers the protocol surface, server-side commit log, client SDK contract, and minimal migration hooks for existing batch and streaming import paths. Background: current ingestion paths (streaming uploader and batch import) suffer edge-case duplication, complex client-side checkpointing, and suboptimal retries when the network or workers fail. We need a contract that allows producers to push variable-sized chunks, receive stable acknowledgements for persisted sequence ranges, and safely resume without producing duplicates or reordering payloads that would invalidate downstream reranking or dedup pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: API: New /v2/embeddings/streams endpoint accepting append-only chunks and returning stable commit offsets
Exactly-once semantics at the record-id level within a stream using idempotency_key + sequence window
Server-side lightweight write-ahead commit log persisted to durable store with purging policy configurable per customer
Clients can resume from last acknowledged commit offset and replay safely with bounded duplicate detection
Async job mode: /v2/embeddings/jobs that accepts a manifest and produces a job id with status polling and webhooks
Retry semantics documented and implemented with exponential backoff and server-side dedup based on idempotency_key
Performance: single-stream ingest scales linearly to target throughput (100k embeddings/min) with end-to-end p50 latency under 500ms for small batches
Integration tests that simulate partial failures, leader restarts, network partitions, and confirm no lost or double-applied records
Observability: per-stream metrics (ingest rate, commit lag, dedup rate) surfaced in Console and linked to a dashboard
technical_notes: Append-only stream model: producer opens stream -> server returns stream_id -> producer sends chunks with increasing sequence numbers -> server persists append and returns commit_offset
Idempotency: combined key of stream_id + idempotency_key for de-duplication; server keeps a sliding window of seen idempotency_keys per stream using compacted store
Commit offset semantics: offset is monotonic per stream and represents byte/record commit boundary safe to resume from
Storage: use existing commit-log tier (Kafka-compatible or durable WAL) with a small metadata layer in PrimaryDB for quick offset lookups and GC markers
Async job mode: supports large manifests (GCS/S3 pointers) and splits into substreams for parallel workers with orchestrator tracking job-state and backpressure
Backpressure: server signals Accept / Throttle with Retry-After and max in-flight chunk count per stream enforced by control plane
Exactly-once per record must be best-effort for very large retention windows; for strict guarantees customers can enable dedupe-store with stronger retention at cost
Ordering: ordering is only guaranteed per-stream at the sequence number level. Cross-stream ordering is not provided; downstream reranking must be tolerant or use single-stream for ordered flows
Compatibility: existing streaming uploader clients should be able to opt into new protocol via header X-Embed-Protocol: append-v2 while old endpoints stay supported for a deprecation period
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy server-side implementation behind feature flag; enable for internal teams and one opt-in customer; expose metrics and enable detailed tracing
Phase 2 (beta): enable SDK clients (python/js) with default opt-out; gather latencies, dedup stats, and edge-case failures; iterate on idempotency TTL and GC
Phase 3 (general): flip default for new customers; provide migration tooling to replay existing batch manifests into new job API
Rollback: server can translate append-v2 to legacy ingest temporarily and reject new streams if unhealthy; orchestrator keeps job checkpoints to resume after rollback
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-customer and global panels for ingest rate, commit lag, failed chunks/sec, dedupe rate, client resumptions
SLOs: commit latency p50 < 250ms, p95 < 1s for small chunks; job completion 95% within expected duration buckets
Alerts: stream_commit_lag > Xs sustained for 2m, dedupe_rate > 0.5% over 10m, job_failure_rate > 1% over 15m
Audit logs: record every commit_offset acknowledge and dedup event for forensic replay
testing_plan: Unit tests for commit log write/read, idempotency window eviction, and offset calculation
Integration tests with durable store failure injection and orchestrator restarts
Chaos tests: kill worker mid-chunk, simulate duplicate chunk submission, and validate no double-apply
Load tests for single-stream and multi-stream scenarios to validate throughput and tail latency
End-to-end reranking pipeline test that verifies scores remain stable after resume/retry scenarios
